summary: Douglas County, OR L-5 cab dated 1933 in the Umpqua NF; removed or destroyed about 1958; no source describes the site today.

facts.status_note: Cab removed (register) or destroyed (firelookout.com) about 1958; no source describes the site since

events.note: L-5 cab dated 1933 by the register and firelookout.com
Panorama photographs taken August 2, 1933; a September 1933 newspaper said the CCC would build a 10-by-10 lookout before snow
Register says removed about 1958; firelookout.com says destroyed about 1958

evidence.supports: L-5 cab built in 1933, removed about 1958
evidence.quote: Built in 1933, this L-5 cab was removed about 1958.

evidence.supports: southwest slope 2.5 miles WSW of Garwood Lookout
evidence.quote: It was located on a southwest slope 2 1/2 miles west southwest of Garwood Lookout.

evidence.supports: L-5 cab built in 1933, destroyed about 1958
evidence.quote: This L-5 cab, built in 1933, was destroyed about 1958.

evidence.supports: September 1933 newspaper: 10-by-10 lookout to be built by the CCC before snow; standard size for secondary lookouts
evidence.quote: A 10 x 10 lookout is to be constructed by the CCC before the snow flies. The 10 x 10 is the standard size for secondary lookouts.

evidence.supports: nearest water a stream about a quarter mile east
evidence.quote: The water source was a stream about a quarter of a mile east of the lookout.

evidence.supports: agency is the U.S. Forest Service
newspaper named in the September 1933 item (Roseburg Chieftain)

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register says the cab was removed about 1958; firelookout.com says it was destroyed about 1958. The story reports both and notes that both date the end to about 1958.

notes_for_editor: Thin record: two one-line register entries plus a short Forest Lookouts clipping. The September 1933 CCC plan may or may not describe the same cab; the sources do not say. No staffing, fire or present-day information was found, so none is written. Brief's kind 'ground' is consistent with an L-5 cab, but no source says ground-level in so many words.
